ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 driver-cancellation fee; close the rider's refund request with a written explanation of the NS-1 wait computation (185 s post-tap inside 200 m).
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a completed driver-side cancellation with a $6.61 cancellation fee on the record, so it enters through NS-0's cancelled_by = driver branch and is tested by NS-1 [F4][F7][NS-0]. The arrival confirmation is a driver tap ("I'm Here") at 09:54:15, at which moment the GPS placed the driver 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m radius — NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied [F6][F1][NS-1].

Requirement (iii) is the whole case. The policy counts only the continuous wait inside the radius after the arrival confirmation, and the trace measures 185 s (3 min 5 s) continuously within 200 m after the 09:54:15 tap, against a 3:01 threshold — the wait exceeds three minutes, so NS-1 (iii) holds [F6][NS-1]. The rider's argument that the pre-tap time must be excluded is correct as a matter of policy [F2][F3][NS-1], but exclusion does not help her: the post-tap figure itself clears the threshold by five seconds, and the record carries no no_show_threshold_min, so the official sample's 8-minute figure she cites is inapplicable [F5][NS-1]. The driver's statement that he waited "more than 3 minutes" [F12] adds nothing either way; the system record independently sustains the wait, so the statement is not doing the work [F6][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (i)–(iii) are all met, no refund trigger under NS-2 fires and the $6.61 stands; the correct outcome is no_action [F7][NS-2]. No other line of the fare is in issue: the charge carries no surge and the record shows no traffic or weather circumstances bearing on it [F8][F13][F14][F15][FARE-1].

The rider's account-review request under NS-2 fails on its own terms. NS-2's flag_account attaches to a driver who tapped "I'm Here" while the GPS showed him outside the pickup radius — here the tap was 40 m out, inside the radius, so the fraud/abuse trigger is not engaged [F1][F6][NS-2]. The driver's history (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days) [F17] is offered only as a basis for an extra action and, under RD-6's "repeated" logic, that action flows from a case upheld AGAINST the driver; this case is not upheld against him, so no flag is warranted, and profile facts cannot decide or add an action here in any event [F17][RD-6]. Likewise the rider's own clean profile [F16] does not affect the computation.

Safety: I read both chat messages, the driver's written statement and the complaint in full. The messages are a pickup notice ("At the pickup now, grey Kia Niro") and a closing notice ("Waited more than 3 min, cancelling") [F9][F10][F12]; the complaint is a billing grievance, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — safety screen: none [SAFE-1].

Evidence: the wait is settled by the GPS and timeline records — the trace shows no sampling hole between the arrival confirmation and the cancellation, the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F2][F6][F11], and the arithmetic driving the outcome (185 s vs 180 s) is on a measured record. No record needed by any cited clause is missing, so evidence_status = sufficient.

Correct that pre-tap time is excluded, but the exclusion is what leaves the controlling figure at 185 s inside 200 m after the 09:54:15 tap, which is still more than 3 minutes [F3][F6][NS-1].
NS-2's refund trigger does not fire: the tap was made 40 m from the pickup (inside the radius) and the post-tap in-radius wait exceeded 3 minutes, so the fee is valid [F1][F6][F7][NS-2].

NS-1 imposes no advance-notice-of-intent requirement, and the chat, which is complete and timestamped and shows the driver at the pickup and waiting, does not excuse the charge [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

NS-2's flag_account attaches only where the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while the GPS showed him outside the pickup radius; here the tap was 40 m out, and profile facts cannot create an account action absent a case upheld against the driver [F1][F6][F17][RD-6][NS-2].

The driver's notice argument is not needed to sustain the fee and is not what decides it; NS-1 turns on the measured arrival confirmation and continuous in-radius wait, not on messages sent to the rider [F9][F10][F6][NS-1].

The driver's conclusion of no_action is correct, but his reasoning rests on the 3 min 55 s platform-arrival figure; that is not the NS-1 baseline — the controlling figure is the 185 s post-tap inside 200 m [F5][F6][NS-1].
